A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MVU research and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The main text and Appendices A-L can be matched reliably; v5 adds Appendix M.

before.justification: v3 reports original MVU evaluations on video-QA and robotics action-recognition datasets, together with component, prompting, and frame-count ablations.

after.justification: v5 retains those original experiments and adds the authors' robot-control success rates in Table A.12. The control baselines are explicitly attributed to prior work.

M1.justification: Appendix M introduces MVU-R, a substantive adaptation from answering questions to controlling a robot. It adds VLM predictions of the next gripper position, depth-augmented information fusion, LLM-generated 3D targets, and mapping to robot actions. The original video-QA procedure remains unchanged.

E1.justification: v5 extends evaluation from video understanding, including Open X-Embodiment action recognition, to interactive manipulation in MetaWorld. Table A.12 reports Door-Open, Door-Close, Basket-Ball, and Shelf-Place, introducing substantially different task requirements. Existing dataset coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Table A.12 adds a distinct robot-control comparison suite: BC-Scratch, BC-R3M, UniPi, AVDC, and LTM. Their scores are taken from prior work and compared with MVU-R, with training differences identified. Existing video-QA comparator sets, including LVNet, remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The new control experiment introduces sequential simulator interaction, simulator-provided depth, task-specific prompting, and task-success rates. It compares training-free MVU-R with policies trained on demonstrations. This adds a substantially different evaluation design; the existing video-QA settings are retained.

E4.justification: Table A.12 adds a limited diagnostic comparison separating door tasks from tasks requiring grasping, exposing zero success on Basket-Ball and Shelf-Place. Existing ablations remain unchanged. Appendix M.3 discusses prompt sensitivity but adds no measured prompt-sensitivity study.

E5.justification: The retained experiments use unchanged point-estimate reporting. The new control results likewise provide percentages without trial counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or other uncertainty estimates; no statistical reporting procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results are unchanged, but Table A.12 adds a new family of control outcomes and comparator scores. MVU achieves 66.7% on Door-Open, 77.3% on Door-Close, and 0.0% on both Basket-Ball and Shelf-Place. These are new task results, not improvements over v3 under matched settings.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and likelihood-selection derivations, including Equations 1-5, are retained. The robot-control extension is described procedurally and introduces no new formal assumptions, propositions, proofs, or mathematical analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract, three stated contributions, and conclusion retain their central claims about modality-constrained performance, likelihood selection, and object-centric MVU. The introduction adds a robot-control reference as further support for the existing robotics-generality claim.

C2.justification: Appendix M interprets the new results as evidence of potential for general-purpose embodied agents. Appendix M.3 adds concrete qualifications: extensive prompt hand-crafting, missing grasper awareness, and inability to perform intelligent grasping. Existing interpretations of the video-QA results remain intact.

D1.justification: Appendices M.1-M.2 document the control prompt, depth handling, and source of the low-level action mapping. The reproducibility statement changes from planned release to stated public code availability, although v3 already listed the repository. Appendix C expands documentation of the existing LVNet implementation.

R1.justification: v5 adds MetaWorld, AVDC, and LTM references and positions the control extension relative to these works and the already-cited LLaRA. The main related-work discussion remains substantially unchanged. The two LLaRA bibliography entries represent the same work.

P1.justification: v5 makes localized grammatical and terminology edits, reorganizes Section 5.2 into action-recognition and robot-control paragraphs, adds Appendix M with three subsections, and expands acknowledgments. The existing narrative and appendix organization are largely preserved.

P2.justification: v5 adds the robot-control pipeline diagram in Figure A.1 and the comparison table A.12. Figures 1-2 receive small caption refinements, and some text reflows. Existing diagrams and table structures are retained without a broader visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v5 adds useful control evidence and explicit failure boundaries to the earlier robotics-generality argument while preserving the video-QA evidence. Implementation details also improve documentation. The gain is limited by sparse control-evaluation reporting: prose and caption describe two tasks while Table A.12 contains four, and trial counts and uncertainty are absent.
